ready1_open_rewrite.title: SciVerse open question
ready1_open_rewrite.rewritten_question_text: According to the data in Figure 2, when $DRKFR$ is not expressed in the cells, the Fursilla (FRSL) transcription level increases. This most likely indicates how $DRKFR$ affects the transcription of FRSL?
ready1_open_rewrite.expected_answer: $DRKFR$ competes with RNA polymerase for binding sites.

claims.canonical_value: Because Fursilla transcript levels increase when $DRKFR$ is unexpressed in the cell, $DRKFR$ must compete for the binding site of RNA polymerase

ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: According to the data in Figure 2, when $DRKFR$ is not expressed in the cells, the Fursilla (FRSL) transcription level increases. This most likely indicates how $DRKFR$ affects the transcription of FRSL?
ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_answer: $DRKFR$ competes with RNA polymerase for binding sites.
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: In Figure 2, the x-axis of the bar chart on the left is the protein overexpressed in the cells, and the y-axis is the mRNA level of the Fursilla transcript; NEFR is about 500, DRKFR is about 100, and LSFR is about 800. The x-axis of the bar chart on the right of Figure 2 is the protein not expressed in the cells, and the y-axis is also the mRNA level of the Fursilla transcript; NEFR is about 500, DRKFR is about 700, and LSFR is about 100. Then reason: when DRKFR is overexpressed, the FRSL transcript is very low, while when DRKFR is not expressed, the FRSL transcript increases, indicating that the presence of DRKFR inhibits FRSL transcription. Combined with the transcription initiation mechanism, the most likely way is that DRKFR occupies or competes for the site that RNA polymerase needs to bind, thereby preventing RNA polymerase from effectively initiating FRSL transcription.
